s1.syndrome_frame: persistent unilateral conjunctival mass with foreign body sensation
salient_findings: persistent foreign body sensation in one eye
linear, soft-tissue lesion along the lower conjunctival fornix
key_facts: no relief with sodium hyaluronate drops
no personal or family history of systemic diseases
linear, soft-tissue lesion along the lower conjunctival fornix
mass isodense to muscle on orbital computed tomography

shortlist.label: Conjunctival Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: persistent unilateral conjunctival mass with foreign body sensation

shortlist.label: Conjunctival Kaposi's Sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: linear, soft-tissue lesion along the lower conjunctival fornix

shortlist.label: Conjunctival Amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: mass isodense to muscle on orbital computed tomography

shortlist.label: Conjunctival Granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: unremarkable routine blood tests and normal visual acuity

shortlist.label: Conjunctival Pyogenic Granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: rapid growth and foreign body sensation

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms and examination findings, including a linear, soft-tissue lesion along the lower conjunctival fornix and a mass isodense to muscle on orbital computed tomography, are consistent with Conjunctival Amyloidosis. The lack of relief with sodium hyaluronate drops and the absence of systemic disease history also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Conjunctival Lymphoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with a salmon pink mass, which is not described in this case

rejected.label: Conjunctival Kaposi's Sarcoma
rejected.why: Usually associated with systemic disease, such as HIV or immunosuppression, which is not present in this case

rejected.label: Conjunctival Granuloma
rejected.why: Would likely have a more rapid onset and be associated with inflammation or infection, which is not described

rejected.label: Conjunctival Pyogenic Granuloma
rejected.why: Typically presents with a rapidly growing, bleeding mass, which is not consistent with the patient's 1-year history of symptoms
